hinweis: Englische Fassung. Schluessel wie data/techniken.json. Texte fachlich aus DE und den englischen Tipps abgeleitet (16.10.2026).

guertel.name: White belt
guertel.kannst_du: You test flows, read the inputs and outputs of every action and format dates directly.
guertel.erreicht_satz: You know the designer and test before you turn a flow on.

guertel.name: Yellow belt
guertel.kannst_du: You write your first expressions, filter and clean up arrays and test loops with just a few items.
guertel.erreicht_satz: You write expressions that hold up even with incomplete data.

guertel.name: Orange belt
guertel.kannst_du: You catch errors with scopes, control concurrent runs and return data to Power Apps.
guertel.erreicht_satz: You control what happens on errors, waiting times and parallel runs.

guertel.name: Green belt
guertel.kannst_du: You process messy data safely, speed up loops and call SharePoint and Microsoft Graph directly.
guertel.erreicht_satz: You build flows that cope with real, messy data.

guertel.name: Blue belt
guertel.kannst_du: You read the real error message from a scope and pass it on to people or agents.
guertel.erreicht_satz: You know why a run fails without opening the run history.

guertel.name: Brown belt
guertel.kannst_du: You keep processes alive for weeks, even beyond the run duration limit of a flow.
guertel.erreicht_satz: You build processes that live longer than a single flow run.

guertel.name: Black belt
guertel.kannst_du: Flows as tools for agents: routers and calls that correct themselves.
guertel.erreicht_satz: You build flows that agents can rely on.

quiz.frage: When do you switch Filter array to Advanced Mode?
antworten: When several conditions belong in one filter
When you want to sort the items by a field
When the filter should run directly in SharePoint
erklaerungen: Correct. In Advanced Mode you write the condition as an expression and combine several checks with and() or or().
Wrong. Filter array removes items but does not sort them. The order stays the same.
Wrong. Filter array works inside the flow on an array that is already loaded, not in the data source.

3.lernziel: You filter arrays with your own expressions in Advanced Mode.
3.kurztext: In basic mode, the Filter array action offers one condition with a field, an operator and a value. In many cases that is not enough: two conditions at once, an OR combination or a comparison with a calculated value. Instead of chaining several filters, you switch to Advanced Mode. There you write the condition as an expression and combine functions such as equals(), contains(), and() and or(). You can also include dynamic content from earlier actions. Everything stays in a single action, and the flow becomes easier to read. The designer still shows simple comparisons as fields.
3.wann_ja: When you want to combine several conditions or compare against calculated values.
3.wann_nein: When a single comparison is enough. Basic mode then stays easier to read.
3.fehler: Chaining several Filter array actions when one expression with and() does the same in a single step.

quiz.frage: What is a JSON viewer extension for when you work with flows?
antworten: Show raw JSON in a readable, structured way
Repair broken flows automatically
Convert JSON into premium connectors
erklaerungen: The extension indents raw JSON from a run and lets you expand and collapse it. That way you find the property you need in your expression.

4.lernziel: You read JSON from runs faster and find the right properties.

quiz.frage: Where does an email address go that never changes during the flow?
antworten: In a variable, so the flow runs faster
In a Compose action or in Parse JSON
In a separate Condition at the start of the flow
erklaerungen: Wrong. A variable does not make the flow faster. Inside loops it even stops Apply to each from running in parallel.
Correct. Fixed values need no variable. Compose or Parse JSON make it clear that the value does not change.
Wrong. A Condition checks something and branches. It is not meant for storing a fixed value.

5.lernziel: You use variables only for values that actually change.
5.titel: Fixed values in Compose instead of variables
5.kurztext: Many flows start with a row of Initialize variable actions for values that never change: an email address, a list URL, a threshold. Fixed values do not need a variable. A single value goes into a Compose action. Several related values go into Parse JSON as one JSON object, and you read them with an expression like outputs('Parse_JSON')?['settingName']. The flow gets shorter, and everyone sees right away that these values are fixed. There is also a practical reason: when you set a variable inside a loop, Apply to each can only run sequentially. Keep variables for values that really change during the run, such as a running total.
5.wann_ja: For settings that stay the same during the run: addresses, URLs, thresholds, texts.
5.wann_nein: For values that change during the run, such as a total or an array you fill step by step. That is what variables are for.
5.fehler: Marking fields as required in the Parse JSON schema that are sometimes missing. The run then fails on schema validation.

quiz.frage: What does the expression utcNow('dd.MM.yyyy') return?
antworten: The current time in Swiss local time
An error, because formatDateTime() is missing
Today's date in the format day.month.year
erklaerungen: Wrong. The format contains no hours, and utcNow() always works in UTC, not in Swiss time.
Wrong. The expression is valid. utcNow() formats by itself, so the second function is not needed.
Correct. utcNow() accepts the format as a parameter, so you do not need formatDateTime() for it.

6.lernziel: You format the current date with a single expression.
6.titel: Format the date directly in utcNow()
6.kurztext: Many flows need today's date in a specific format, for a file name or a subject line, for example. Often you find formatDateTime(utcNow(), 'format') in the flow for this. There is a shorter way: utcNow() accepts the format directly as a parameter. utcNow('dd.MM.yyyy') returns the date as day.month.year, without a second function. The result is the same, and the expression is shorter and easier to read. Watch the upper and lower case in the format string: MM stands for the month, mm for the minute. And utcNow() always returns the time in UTC. If you need local time, convert it with convertTimeZone().
6.wann_ja: When you need the current point in time in a fixed format, for file names, subject lines or logs, for example.
6.wann_nein: When you format a date from a list or an email. For that, formatDateTime() with the value from the source is still the right choice.
6.fehler: Writing mm instead of MM in the format. The date then shows the minute instead of the month.

quiz.frage: What does union() return when you pass the same array twice?
antworten: The array without duplicate entries
The array twice, one after the other
Only the entries that appear twice
erklaerungen: Correct. union() returns each value only once, so union(x, x) works like DISTINCT.
Wrong. That would be simple concatenation. union() removes the duplicates.
Wrong. union() combines the arrays and keeps each value once, including those that appear only once.

7.lernziel: You create unique values with union() and then filter them with Filter array.
7.kurztext: When you merge data from two sources, duplicate entries quickly end up in the result. The union() function combines two arrays and returns each value only once. That leads to a simple trick: pass the same array twice, union(x, x), and you get the array back without duplicates, like DISTINCT in a database. This works with simple values and with objects. Then you narrow the result down with Filter array to the entries you need. Two built-in steps replace a loop with a condition and a variable. If you need to keep the duplicates, union() is the wrong choice.
7.wann_ja: When you merge lists or want to clean up an array before you continue.
7.wann_nein: When duplicate entries must be kept, for example bookings with the same amount.
7.fehler: Removing duplicates in a loop with a condition and a variable, although a single expression is enough.

quiz.frage: What does an automated backup of flows and apps build on?
antworten: Scheduled exports of the solution as a ZIP file
A copy of every flow in the owner's mailbox
The action outputs stored in the run history
erklaerungen: Flows and apps sit in a solution, and a scheduled flow exports it regularly as a ZIP to SharePoint, OneDrive or Azure Blob. You import that file again when you need to restore.

8.lernziel: You set up a recurring backup of your solutions.

quiz.frage: What does a test run show you that you don't otherwise see in the designer?
antworten: The number of licenses your flow consumes
The inputs and outputs of every single action
A list of all people who use the flow
erklaerungen: Wrong. A test run checks the logic of your flow. It tells you nothing about licensing.
Correct. In a test run you open each action and see which values it received and returned.
Wrong. The test run shows the path of the data through your flow, not a list of users.

9.lernziel: You test a flow before turning it on and read the results of every action.
9.titel: Test a flow before it goes live
9.kurztext: A new flow rarely runs without errors on the first try. With Test in the designer you start it manually, provide the trigger inputs yourself and follow the run step by step. For every action you see what goes in and what comes out. That way you find the step where a value stays empty or an expression returns something other than expected, before real data runs through the flow. Then you adjust it and test again, as often as you like. Only when the inputs and outputs are right do you turn the flow on for daily use.
9.wann_ja: Before every activation and after every change to the trigger, expressions or conditions.
9.wann_nein: When an action sends real emails or changes data you don't want to touch. Give it a static result first.
9.fehler: Looking only at the green check mark without opening the outputs. Succeeded does not mean the value is right.

quiz.frage: What do you replace before pasting a Filter array expression as a trigger condition?
antworten: The leading @ character with a # character
Nothing, the expression works unchanged
item() with triggerOutputs() or triggerBody()
erklaerungen: Filter array evaluates each element with item(), which does not exist in a trigger. In the trigger condition you therefore reference triggerOutputs() or triggerBody().

11.lernziel: You write trigger conditions so the flow only starts on matching events.

quiz.frage: What do you check after pasting from My clipboard?
antworten: The licenses of everyone who uses the flow
Whether the Scope was deleted in the old flow
Connections and dynamic content from the old flow
erklaerungen: Wrong. Copying and pasting does not change any license. It is about the settings of the pasted actions.
Wrong. Copying leaves the Scope in the old flow unchanged. Both flows keep their actions.
Correct. Connections are not copied, and references to actions of the old flow do not resolve in the new one.

12.lernziel: You use Scopes as reusable building blocks.
12.kurztext: Some blocks show up in almost every flow: a notification, a log entry, an error message. Instead of clicking them together again each time, you put the actions in a Scope and choose Copy to my clipboard from the Scope's menu. In the next flow you find the block in the action picker under My clipboard and paste it with all its settings. Afterwards you check two things: connections are not copied, so you reconnect the actions. And dynamic content that pointed to the trigger or earlier actions of the old flow needs to be mapped again. My clipboard is tied to your browser. For building blocks a whole team uses, a child flow is the better choice.
12.wann_ja: For blocks you build again and again yourself, such as an error message or a log entry.
12.wann_nein: For building blocks that several people should use. My clipboard is tied to your browser, a child flow fits better here.
12.fehler: Running the pasted block without resetting the references to the trigger and earlier actions.

quiz.frage: How do you set Configure run after on the Catch scope?
antworten: has failed and has timed out on, is successful off
Tick all four statuses so Catch always runs
Tick only is successful so Catch follows Try
erklaerungen: Correct. That way Catch only runs when something in the Try scope fails or takes too long.
Wrong. That is how you set up Finally. Catch would otherwise also start after every successful run.
Wrong. Then Catch would only run when everything works, exactly when there is nothing to catch.

15.lernziel: You build the try-catch-finally pattern into every important flow.
15.titel: Catch errors with Try, Catch and Finally
15.kurztext: Without error handling, a flow stops at the first failing action, and nobody finds out. With three scopes you rebuild the pattern from programming. The Try scope holds the actual logic. The Catch scope runs only when Try fails: under Configure run after you tick has failed and has timed out and leave is successful unchecked. There you notify someone or write a log entry. The Finally scope always runs, with all four statuses ticked, and cleans up. With result('Try') you read in Catch which action failed. If the run should show as failed in the run history, add a Terminate action with the status Failed in Catch.
15.wann_ja: In every flow whose failure someone needs to notice: interfaces, files, records in Dataverse.
15.wann_nein: In a short test flow that you start yourself and whose run you follow directly.
15.fehler: Leaving critical actions outside the Try scope. Catch never sees what fails there.

quiz.frage: What do you get from Format data by example or its successor, the Copilot expression assistant?
antworten: A ready-made template for the whole flow
A new data source with formatted values
The matching expression for your example
erklaerungen: You give an example or describe the format you want, and Power Automate generates the expression, for example formatDateTime() for a date. The classic feature has been replaced by the Copilot expression assistant.

17.lernziel: You let Power Automate generate formatting expressions instead of writing them from memory.

quiz.frage: How do you save a password-protected file from the web?
antworten: Authenticated HTTP request, then "Create file"
Only "Upload file from URL" with the file URL
"Get file content" directly with the web address
erklaerungen: An HTTP request with authentication fetches the protected content, and "Create file" saves it. "Upload file from URL" only suits public files.

18.lernziel: You download files from the web with the right action, depending on how they are protected.

quiz.frage: What does a flow have to be so you can change its owner directly?
antworten: Turned off
Solution-aware
A child flow
erklaerungen: If the flow is in a solution, you change the owner directly under Details. Connections and run history stay intact.

20.lernziel: You hand flows over cleanly to a new owner.

quiz.frage: In a manually triggered flow, where do you find the email address of the person who started it?
antworten: In outputs('Compose')?['body']
In triggerOutputs()?['headers']
In workflow()?['run']?['name']
erklaerungen: The manual trigger returns x-ms-user-email among its headers. You read the address with triggerOutputs()?['headers']?['x-ms-user-email'].

21.lernziel: You use trigger headers to notify the person who started the flow.

quiz.frage: How do you merge two arrays and keep the duplicates?
antworten: join(), concat() and then split()
union() with both arrays as parameters
intersection() with both arrays
erklaerungen: union() removes duplicate items. With join() both arrays become text, concat() appends them and split() turns the result back into an array.

24.lernziel: You choose between union() and the join-concat-split pattern depending on what you need.

quiz.frage: How do you make the Overwrite toggle visible in Create file?
antworten: Turn off Allow chunking in the settings
Turn on Concurrency control in the settings
Delete the existing file first with Delete file
erklaerungen: As long as chunking is on, Create file hides the Overwrite toggle. Without chunking it appears, but very large files can then fail.

27.lernziel: You overwrite existing files in SharePoint without a workaround.

quiz.frage: Why do you add a description property to the Parse JSON schema?
antworten: It validates incoming data more strictly against the schema
It shows in Dynamic content and tells same-named fields apart
It automatically makes the field required in the schema
erklaerungen: The description appears in Dynamic content below the field. This lets you tell apart two fields with the same name.

29.lernziel: You make Dynamic content from Parse JSON clearly readable.

quiz.frage: What does coalesce() return?
antworten: The last value in the parameter list
The first value that is not null
All values joined into one text
erklaerungen: coalesce() checks the values in order and returns the first one that is not null. In Power Automate an empty string does not count as null.

33.lernziel: You replace nested empty checks with coalesce().

quiz.frage: What is an advantage of the PowerApps V2 trigger?
antworten: It works without any connection to data sources
It starts the flow automatically on a schedule
Typed inputs such as text, number or yes/no
erklaerungen: You set the type for every input, for example text, number, yes/no, email or date. The title and description of each input appear in Power Apps when you call Run().

34.lernziel: You use the PowerApps V2 trigger with clear inputs for app flows.

quiz.frage: What happens to new trigger events with a parallelism of 1?
antworten: They are discarded immediately and never run
They wait until the current run has finished
They still run in parallel, just more slowly
erklaerungen: Wrong. New trigger events wait. Whether each one becomes a run is only uncertain once the queue is full.
Correct. Further runs wait in a queue and start one after another.
Wrong. With a parallelism of 1, exactly one run is active at a time, all others wait.

35.lernziel: You prevent conflicts by letting flow instances run one after another.
35.kurztext: An automated flow starts on every new event, even if the previous run has not finished yet. When two runs work on the same data at the same time, you get duplicates, or one run overwrites the other. In the trigger settings you turn on Concurrency Control and set the degree of parallelism to 1. Then only one run is active at a time, further runs wait and start in order. That costs time but protects the data. The queue is limited: at most {limit:trigger_warteschlange} runs can wait. And think before you do it: you can only turn off Concurrency Control on the trigger by deleting the trigger and adding it again.
35.wann_ja: When several runs work on the same list, the same file or the same counter.
35.wann_nein: When a large number of events arrive in a short time. The queue is limited, and one run after the other becomes a bottleneck.
35.fehler: Turning on Concurrency Control on the trigger just to try it out. The only way back is to delete the trigger and add it again.

quiz.frage: What does Static Result do to an action?
antworten: It runs, but its output is not saved
It only runs when you start the flow manually
It returns a fixed output without running
erklaerungen: Wrong. With Static Result the action does not run at all. That is exactly why it changes no data.
Wrong. Static Result does not depend on how the flow starts. It applies to every run as long as it is turned on.
Correct. The action counts as successful and passes on the predefined result without actually running.

36.lernziel: You test flows with simulated results without changing real data.
36.titel: Test with Static Result without changing data
36.kurztext: Some actions you don't want to actually run while testing: they send emails, change records or take a long time. With Static Result you give an action a fixed result. In the designer you turn on Enable Static Result in the Testing section of the action and define which output it should return. On the next run the action counts as successful without being executed. The following steps continue with your predefined output. That way you test the logic after it calmly and with different cases, without touching real data. Before the flow goes into production, you turn the static result off again.
36.wann_ja: For actions that send emails, change data or take long, while you test the steps after them.
36.wann_nein: In production. If Static Result stays on, the flow never actually runs the action.
36.fehler: Leaving Static Result on after testing. The flow reports success although the action never ran.

quiz.frage: What do you gain by turning a Name/Value table into a JSON object?
antworten: Direct access to every entry by its name
An automatic translation of all values in the table
A faster query of the SharePoint list in the flow
erklaerungen: Instead of looping through the table and comparing every name, you read the value directly by its name after Parse JSON.

37.lernziel: You make configuration tables directly addressable in a flow.

quiz.frage: Where do you use FetchXML in a flow?
antworten: In the Fetch Xml Query parameter of the List rows action
In the trigger condition of the Dataverse trigger
In a separate FetchXML action of the Dataverse connector
erklaerungen: List rows accepts FetchXML directly in the Fetch Xml Query parameter, no separate action is needed. This enables joins and grouping that the OData filter cannot do.

39.lernziel: You let Dataverse calculate complex queries and totals on the server.

quiz.frage: Which step finally removes all collected apps and flows at once?
antworten: Exporting as a managed solution
Deleting the unmanaged solution
Deleting the imported managed solution
erklaerungen: After the re-import the apps and flows belong to the managed solution. Deleting it removes all its components in one step, without further confirmation.

40.lernziel: You clean up test apps and flows in one go.

quiz.frage: According to the tip, what do you use Scopes for?
antworten: To trigger other flows from the running flow
To group actions and isolate errors
To store variables across several runs
erklaerungen: A Scope bundles actions into one block. If something fails inside it, you react to the whole block, and you can copy the block into other flows.

45.lernziel: You structure flows into readable blocks with Scopes.

quiz.frage: How many operations does one SharePoint $batch call bundle at most?
erklaerungen: The SharePoint REST API accepts up to 1000 create, update or delete operations in one $batch call. Instead of hundreds of single actions you send one HTTP request.

47.lernziel: You process large numbers of SharePoint items with batch calls instead of single actions.

quiz.frage: Which way brings a flow to colleagues together with its dependencies?
antworten: Send them a screenshot
Package it in a solution
Share the run history
erklaerungen: A solution bundles apps, flows, connection references and tables. On export and import the dependencies move along.

48.lernziel: You choose the right way to share flows with others.

quiz.frage: Which status does the Do Until loop report when Count or Timeout ends it?
antworten: TimedOut
Succeeded
Cancelled
erklaerungen: Even when Count or Timeout stops the loop, it reports Succeeded. That is why you check the variable after the loop to see whether the wait worked.

49.lernziel: You build polling loops with a Delay and check the result in the variable, not in the loop status.

quiz.frage: Why do you need an overview of which flow calls which?
antworten: To save licenses for child flows
For the right order during deployment
To delete unused flows automatically
erklaerungen: Child flows must exist and be turned on in the target environment before you activate the parent flow. The overview shows you this order and which flows a change affects.

51.lernziel: You document parent-child dependencies between flows.

quiz.frage: When do you use the HTTP actions in Power Automate?
antworten: Only for testing flows before going live
For every query on a SharePoint list
When no ready-made connector covers the API
erklaerungen: HTTP actions call any REST API, including Microsoft Graph. You need them where the ready-made connectors fall short.

58.lernziel: You call APIs without a ready-made connector over HTTP.

quiz.frage: What does item()?['id'] return when the property id is missing?
antworten: The value null, and the flow keeps running
An error that stops the action immediately
The value of the previous item in the array
erklaerungen: Correct. The question mark turns a missing property into null instead of failing the action.
Wrong. That happens without the question mark: item()['id'] fails with InvalidTemplate.
Wrong. The expression only reads the current item and takes no values from other items.

59.lernziel: You access properties that may be missing in a robust way.
59.kurztext: Data from lists, emails or APIs is rarely complete. An expression like item()['id'] assumes that the property id always exists. If it is missing in a single item, the action fails with the error InvalidTemplate. With a question mark before the bracket, item()?['id'], the expression returns null in that case instead of an error. The question mark only protects the bracket it stands in front of. For nested paths you therefore put it before every level. Then you decide what should happen with null, for example with coalesce() and a fallback value or with a Condition. The question mark does not help against a wrong data type.
59.wann_ja: Whenever you read data whose fields are not always present, such as API responses or optional list columns.
59.wann_nein: When a missing field is a real error you want to see. Then the action should fail.
59.fehler: Setting the question mark only on the first level. triggerBody()?['missing']['x'] still fails when missing is absent.

quiz.frage: Which problem do environment variables solve?
antworten: Missing licenses for premium connectors
Hardcoded values that differ per environment
Slow loops over large amounts of data
erklaerungen: Environment variables replace hardcoded values. The same solution then moves from Dev through Test to Prod without changes.

61.lernziel: You build flows with environment variables for moving between environments.

quiz.frage: What does PowerDocu need as input?
antworten: An export of your flow, app or solution
Read access to the environment's run history
A premium license for each documented flow
erklaerungen: PowerDocu is a free tool for Windows. You export the flow, app or solution and get documentation in Word, Markdown or HTML.

65.lernziel: You document flows automatically instead of with screenshots.

quiz.frage: According to the tip, how do you turn an array into an object?
antworten: An Apply to each loop with Append to array
The Create HTML table action with custom columns
A Select action and nested replace() expressions
erklaerungen: Select builds the key-value pairs, and the nested replace() expressions remove brackets and separators until a single object remains. You don't need a loop for this.

71.lernziel: You turn arrays into addressable objects without loops.

quiz.frage: When must you not raise the concurrency of a loop?
antworten: When it has to process more than a hundred items
When it increments a variable or appends to an array
When it reads items from a SharePoint list
erklaerungen: Wrong. Concurrency saves the most time precisely when there are many independent items.
Correct. Parallel iterations read and write the same variable at the same time and overwrite each other.
Wrong. The source does not matter. What counts is whether the iterations depend on each other.

75.lernziel: You speed up loops with concurrency and recognize when it corrupts results.
75.titel: Run Apply to each in parallel
75.kurztext: Apply to each processes items one after another by default. With hundreds of items that takes time, even when every iteration stands on its own. In the loop settings you turn on Concurrency control and raise the degree of parallelism to at most {limit:schleife_parallel_max}. Several iterations then run at the same time, and the loop often finishes in a fraction of the time. This only works when the iterations are independent. If the loop increments a counter or appends values to an array, the iterations overwrite each other. In that case build the result with Select or union() instead of variables. Too much parallelism against the same connector can also lead to throttling.
75.wann_ja: When every iteration stands on its own, such as one email per person or one update per record.
75.wann_nein: When iterations change the same variable or the order matters.
75.fehler: Turning on concurrency and still using Increment variable inside the loop. The counter is wrong afterwards.

quiz.frage: How do you keep flow notifications in Teams separated by topic?
antworten: The Flow bot posts to one group chat per topic
All messages are written to a SharePoint list
Everything goes to your personal Flow bot chat
erklaerungen: You create one group chat per topic and let the Flow bot post there with Post message in a chat or channel. That way not every message lands in the same chat.

83.lernziel: You organize flow notifications in Teams by topic.

quiz.frage: What is an action's Code View good for?
antworten: Editing the action directly in JSON
Exporting the whole flow as a file
Reading an action's expressions in full
erklaerungen: Wrong. Code View is read-only. You make changes in the designer or in the expression editor.
Wrong. Code View shows only that one action. It has nothing to do with exporting the flow.
Correct. Code View shows the action's definition with all expressions, exactly as the flow runs them.

89.lernziel: You read an action's definition to find errors faster.
89.titel: Look behind an action with Code View
89.kurztext: In the designer you see fields, icons and dynamic content. What the action really runs is in its definition. From the action's menu with the three dots you open Code View, formerly Peek code. It shows the action as JSON, with all inputs and the complete expressions. You see, for example, that a harmless-looking field hides a nested concat() expression. That helps with debugging and with learning: you see how someone else solved a step and reuse the expression in your own flow. Code View is read-only. You still change the action in the designer.
89.wann_ja: When a field returns something other than expected and you want to see which expression is really behind it.
89.wann_nein: When you want to change something. You do that in the designer, Code View is read-only.
89.fehler: Checking only the visible field in the designer. Only Code View shows the complete expression with all its functions.

quiz.frage: What do you need to keep in mind with the free PDF services?
antworten: Most of the connectors are still premium
They only work with Word files as the source
They need no connection in Power Automate
erklaerungen: Adobe PDF Services, Encodian, Muhimbi and Cloudmersive have free tiers. Their connectors in Power Automate are mostly premium, so you may still need a premium license.

92.lernziel: You choose a PDF service that fits your quota and license.

quiz.frage: Which file in the DOCX archive contains the document's text?
antworten: [Content_Types].xml
docProps/app.xml
word/document.xml
erklaerungen: A DOCX file is a ZIP archive. After extraction, the document's text is in word/document.xml.

quiz.frage: What are the two ? for in outputs('Compose')?[InputValue]?['Title']?
antworten: They prevent an error when a key is unknown
They mark the values as optional inputs

Wrong. The question mark has nothing to do with inputs. It only protects the access to a property.
Wrong. The question mark does not change the type. For text you need string().

100.lernziel: You replace branches with a lookup in a JSON object.
100.kurztext: A Switch with a dozen cases or Conditions nested three levels deep is hard to read, and every new case means changing the structure of the flow. With coalesce() you set a fallback value for unknown keys. You add new cases in the JSON, the flow itself stays the same.
100.wann_ja: When a Switch only looks up values: statuses, texts, addresses or settings per environment.
100.wann_nein: When the cases should trigger different actions. Then Switch remains the right tool.
100.fehler: Not catching unknown keys. Without coalesce(), null travels on and only surfaces much later.

quiz.frage: Parse JSON fails with "Expected String but got Null". What helps?
antworten: Adding the field to the required list as well
Setting the type to a list of string and null
Generating the schema from a new sample response
erklaerungen: Wrong. required only checks whether the field is present. It does not fix the type error on null.
Correct. With ["string", "null"] the schema accepts text and null, and validation passes.
Wrong. A new sample again sets exactly one type per field. The next null fails validation again.

104.lernziel: You write robust schemas for unreliable APIs.
104.titel: A JSON schema that tolerates null
104.kurztext: Parse JSON checks every response against a schema. If you generate the schema from a sample response, the designer sets exactly one type per field, such as string. When a field later arrives as null, the action fails with "Invalid type. Expected String but got Null." The fix is a type list: "type": ["string", "null"] accepts text and null. If a field is sometimes missing entirely, you remove it from the required list. If both can happen, you do both. The exact cause of a failed validation is in the action's outputs in the errors array. The run itself only reports that schema validation failed.
104.wann_ja: For responses from APIs and forms where fields may stay empty.
104.wann_nein: For fields that must never be empty. There the schema validation should fail and show the error.
104.fehler: Reading only the run's error message. The exact cause is in the outputs of Parse JSON in the errors array.

quiz.frage: What does the timeout value P2W on an action mean?
antworten: The action only starts after two weeks
The action runs twice a week
The action waits for two weeks at most
erklaerungen: Wrong. A timeout delays nothing. It defines when a running action counts as timed out.
Wrong. A timeout does not repeat an action. Repetitions are handled by the Retry Policy.
Correct. P2W is a duration in ISO 8601 format and stands for two weeks.

109.lernziel: You protect long approvals against timeouts.
109.titel: Set a timeout for long-running actions
109.kurztext: An approval or another action that waits for people can take longer than planned. In the action settings you define under Timeout how long it may wait at most. You write the duration in ISO 8601 format: P1D is one day, P2W is two weeks, PT2H is two hours. When the time runs out, the action counts as timed out. So that the flow does not simply fail, add an action whose Configure run after is set to has timed out only. There you send a reminder, escalate or start a new request. On top of that, every flow run is limited to {limit:laufzeit_max}.
109.wann_ja: For approvals and other actions that wait for a response whose duration you do not know.
109.wann_nein: When the process can exceed the run duration limit of {limit:laufzeit_max}. A timeout is not enough then, because the whole run ends before.
109.fehler: Setting the timeout but building no path for has timed out. The run then fails anyway.

quiz.frage: Why does /v1.0/me/chats fail with this action, even for admins?
antworten: The token lacks the permission for chats
Chats cannot be read through Graph at all
The Base Resource URL is set incorrectly
erklaerungen: Correct. The connector has a fixed list of permissions. Chats are not on it, and the account's role does not change that.
Wrong. Graph does offer chats. Only the matching permission is missing from this connector's token.
Wrong. With a wrong base URL every call would fail. But /v1.0/me works.

138.lernziel: You call Microsoft Graph from a flow without an app registration.
138.titel: Call Microsoft Graph without an app registration
138.kurztext: To call Microsoft Graph you normally register an app in Microsoft Entra ID and manage secrets or certificates. The action HTTP with Microsoft Entra ID (preauthorized) takes care of that for you. You sign in once and set both Base Resource URL and Resource URI to https://graph.microsoft.com. Then you choose the method and endpoint, for example GET on /v1.0/me, and the connector gets the token itself. The catch: the token carries a fixed list of permissions. Profile, groups, files, mail and calendar work. Chats, presence or sign-in logs do not, not even with an admin role. You get further pages of a response through @odata.nextLink.
138.wann_ja: For Graph queries on behalf of the signed-in person: profile, groups, files, mail, calendar.
138.wann_nein: When you need chats, presence, sign-in logs or Intune, or when you have no premium license.

quiz.frage: Why does the first action set TriggerFlow to No right away?
antworten: So the approval is deleted when it expires
So changes during the run don't trigger a new start
So the approver doesn't receive an email
erklaerungen: Wrong. TriggerFlow only controls when the flow starts. The column has nothing to do with the approval itself.
Correct. Only the path after the timeout sets TriggerFlow back to Yes. That gives exactly one restart per cycle.
Wrong. Whether a new email is sent depends on the chosen method, not on TriggerFlow.

144.lernziel: You build approvals that may stay open for longer than 30 days.
144.kurztext: A flow run ends after {limit:laufzeit_max}. If an approval waits longer, it runs into nothing and nobody notices. The fix: the flow restarts itself. A SharePoint list gets a Yes/No column TriggerFlow. Thanks to a trigger condition, the trigger "When an item is created or modified" only fires when it is Yes, and the first action immediately sets it to No. The approval gets a timeout just below the limit, for example P29D. When it expires, an action that runs after "has timed out" sets TriggerFlow back to Yes, and a new run starts. If you don't want a new email, you split "Create an approval" and "Wait for an approval" and store the approval ID.
144.wann_ja: For contracts, budgets, legal reviews and other decisions that can take longer than a month.
144.wann_nein: When the decision is sure to be made within {limit:laufzeit_max}. Then a timeout with a path for "has timed out" is enough.
144.fehler: Leaving out the trigger condition. Every change to the item then starts a new run, and the flow keeps calling itself.

quiz.frage: How do you protect an apostrophe in an OData filter?
antworten: You encode it with encodeUriComponent()
You put a backslash in front of it
You double it with replace()
erklaerungen: Wrong. encodeUriComponent() belongs in URLs. In an OData filter it breaks the query syntax.
Wrong. A backslash does not escape an apostrophe in OData. The text still ends at that point.
Correct. In OData two apostrophes stand for one apostrophe in the value, and the filter stays valid.

146.lernziel: You stop special characters from breaking filters and requests.
146.titel: Encode apostrophes and special characters correctly
146.kurztext: Special characters in values break queries and requests because the flow reads them as part of the syntax. The right fix depends on where the value goes. In an OData filter like Title eq 'Tom's Diner' the apostrophe ends the text too early. You double it with replace(), so the query reads 'Tom''s Diner'. For values in a URL you use encodeUriComponent(), which turns spaces, question marks and apostrophes into percent codes. You read encoded values from outside back with decodeUriComponent(). For text in the body of a JSON request you build the object with setProperty() and json(). Then the flow escapes quotes, backslashes and line breaks itself.
146.wann_ja: When names, titles or free text end up in filters, URLs or JSON requests.
146.wann_nein: When the value is only displayed or written to a field and is never part of a query or URL.
146.fehler: Using encodeUriComponent() in an OData filter. It encodes the syntax as well, and the query fails.

quiz.frage: What does take(array, 5) return if the array has only three items?
antworten: All three items, without an error
An error, because items are missing
Three items plus two empty ones
erklaerungen: Correct. take() returns at most the given number. If there are fewer, all existing items come back.
Wrong. take() does not fail when the array is shorter than the requested number.
Wrong. take() does not fill anything up. It only cuts off what goes beyond the number.

148.lernziel: You test loops with a few items without restructuring the flow.
148.titel: Shorten loops with take() while testing
148.kurztext: Testing a loop over hundreds of items costs time and actions on every run. With take() you process only the first items while testing. You replace the input of Apply to each with an expression like take(outputs('Select'), 5). The loop then runs exactly five times, no matter how large the array is. If the array has fewer items, take() simply returns all of them, without an error. This way you check the logic inside the loop on a few real records. Once everything works, you remove take() and select the original output again. The structure of the flow stays unchanged.
148.wann_ja: When testing loops over large lists or tables, before you let the flow loose on all data.
148.wann_nein: In production. If take() stays in the flow, it permanently processes only the first items.
148.fehler: Forgetting take() in the flow after testing. A note on the action reminds you to remove it again.

The approval belongs to the mailbox identity, and the person who clicks is not registered as the approver. The solution is the action Send email with options from Office 365 Outlook. You put the shared mailbox in To and the buttons in User Options, for example Approve,Reject. Anyone with access to the mailbox can respond. The answer is in SelectedOption, and UserEmailAddress shows who clicked. This creates no entry in the Approvals center. If you want to trace the decision, you write it to a list yourself.

149.wann_nein: When you need the history in the Approvals center or a specific person has to decide.

quiz.frage: Why do you rename via FileLeafRef instead of copying?
antworten: Copying is never possible in libraries
FileLeafRef also changes the file extension
ID, versions and metadata are kept
erklaerungen: Wrong. Copying works, but it creates a new item with a new ID and no version history.
Wrong. SharePoint ignores a changed extension in FileLeafRef. For that you need MoveTo.
Correct. MERGE on FileLeafRef only changes the name. The item itself stays the same.

153.lernziel: You rename SharePoint files without copying them.
153.titel: Rename a SharePoint file via REST
153.kurztext: The SharePoint connector has no rename action. Copying and deleting creates a new file with a new ID, without version history and metadata. A single call with "Send an HTTP request to SharePoint" is cleaner. You send a POST to the list item of the file and turn it into an update with the headers IF-MATCH: * and X-HTTP-Method: MERGE. The body contains only the FileLeafRef field with the new file name including the extension. With the odata=nometadata headers you don't need a __metadata entry. A 204 response means success. ID, versions, permissions and metadata are kept. You cannot change the file extension this way, MoveTo does that.
153.wann_ja: For naming conventions, reference numbers in the file name or corrections to uploaded files.
153.wann_nein: When the file extension or the folder should change. MoveTo is the right call for that.
153.fehler: Writing the name without the extension into FileLeafRef. The file name always includes the extension.
suchbegriffe: Send an HTTP request to SharePoint

quiz.frage: Which fields does the MERGE call restore?
antworten: AuthorId, EditorId, Created and Modified
The file's permissions and sharing links
Only the file name and the folder path
erklaerungen: Copying and deleting loses the creator, last editor and timestamps. A MERGE through Send an HTTP request to SharePoint writes them back.

154.lernziel: You migrate files without losing their creator and dates.

quiz.frage: What does the expression div(75, 200) return?
antworten: 0, because both values are whole numbers
0.375, because div() always returns decimals
An error, because 75 is smaller than 200
erklaerungen: Correct. With two whole numbers div() does integer division and cuts off the decimals.
Wrong. You only get a decimal when at least one value is a decimal, for example after float().
Wrong. A smaller dividend is not an error. The division would only fail on a divisor of 0.

155.lernziel: You calculate percentages and ratios with correct decimal places.
155.titel: float() before div() for correct decimals
155.kurztext: You calculate a share from two counts and get 0 instead of 37.5. The reason: div() does integer division when both values are whole numbers and cuts off the decimals. div(75, 200) therefore returns 0, and times 100 it stays 0. As soon as one of the two values is a decimal, div() returns a decimal. The safest way is to convert both values with float(). For display you round the result to two places with formatNumber(), but that turns it into text. And protect the division with if() when the divisor can be 0, otherwise the action fails.
155.wann_ja: For percentages, shares and averages from counts or length().
155.wann_nein: When you want a whole number on purpose. Then integer division is correct, div(7, 2) returns 3.
155.fehler: Calculating further with the result of formatNumber(). It is text and needs float() to become a number again.

quiz.frage: How do nested data get from a flow into a canvas app?
antworten: With a separate output for every field
As JSON text in one output, then ParseJSON
Through the Response action of the HTTP connector
erklaerungen: Wrong. Flat outputs cannot represent lists or nested records.
Correct. One text output carries any structure, and ParseJSON rebuilds it in the app.
Wrong. For this case Respond to a Power App or flow is enough. You do not need Response.

158.lernziel: You return nested data to an app without premium.
158.titel: Return flow data to Power Apps as JSON
158.kurztext: A flow often returns more than a single value to a canvas app, for example a customer with all their orders. Respond to a Power App or flow, however, only knows flat outputs like text, number or yes/no. Instead of creating dozens of fields, you build the result in the flow as JSON, for example with Select and Compose, and return it as one single text output. In Power Apps, ParseJSON reads the text back in. Without a type you get a dynamic value and convert fields with Text(), Value() or Boolean(). With a Type as the second argument you get typed records and tables directly. You do not need the Response action from the HTTP connector for this.

158.wann_nein: With very large amounts of data. Then the flow stores the data in SharePoint or Dataverse, and the app reads it directly.

quiz.frage: Which endpoint do you use to create the columns in the target list?
antworten: fields/addfieldasjson
fields/clonefromschema
fields/createfieldasxml
erklaerungen: You POST the SchemaXml of each custom column to fields/createfieldasxml on the target list. That creates the columns with the same internal names and settings.

161.lernziel: You transfer a list's columns exactly to another site.

quiz.frage: What must the members array contain for a private channel?
antworten: Only guest accounts from other tenants
At least one person with the owner role
All members of the parent team
erklaerungen: A private channel needs members when you create it, and at least one of them has roles: ["owner"]. Otherwise Graph rejects the request with a 400.

162.lernziel: You create private Teams channels automatically.

quiz.frage: Which content type does the ICS file get?
antworten: application/pdf
text/calendar
text/plain
erklaerungen: The ICS file is plain text in iCalendar format. When you attach it as text/calendar, the mail client offers to add it to the calendar.

163.lernziel: You send events that anyone can add to their own calendar.

quiz.frage: Which Graph endpoint invites guests?
antworten: /v1.0/users
/v1.0/invitations
/v1.0/groups
erklaerungen: A POST to /v1.0/invitations adds the person as a guest in Microsoft Entra ID. If you want, Graph sends the invitation along with it.

164.lernziel: You invite external people as guests automatically.

quiz.frage: Why are onPremisesSamAccountName and similar fields missing from a normal query?
antworten: They are stored only in Exchange Online
They need a separate license per user
They only come back if $select names them
erklaerungen: Without $select, Graph returns only the default fields. If you name the attributes in $select, they are included.

165.lernziel: You read on-prem AD fields from Graph in a targeted way.

quiz.frage: Which action shows you whether a person is away?
antworten: Office 365 Users: "Get user profile (V2)"
Office 365 Outlook: "Get mail tips for a mailbox (V2)"
Office 365 Outlook: "Get calendar view of events"
erklaerungen: "Get mail tips for a mailbox (V2)" with the automaticReplies option shows whether automatic replies are on. It works without HTTP and without an app registration.

166.lernziel: You redirect approvals to a deputy when the approver is away.

quiz.frage: Is there a dateDiff() function in cloud flow expressions?
antworten: Yes, but only with a premium license
Yes, it returns the difference in days
No, you calculate the difference with ticks()
erklaerungen: dateDiff() does not exist. You subtract the ticks() of both timestamps and divide by 864000000000 to get the days as a number.

167.lernziel: You calculate time differences and compare dates reliably.

quiz.frage: What may result() point to in an expression?
antworten: Any action anywhere in the whole flow
Only the trigger at the start of the flow
A Scope, Apply to each or Until
erklaerungen: Wrong. If result() points to a simple action such as Compose, even saving fails.
Wrong. The trigger contains no actions. result() needs a container with actions inside.
Correct. result() reads the actions inside such a container. If it points to a simple action, the flow cannot be saved.

168.lernziel: You pass the real error message on to people or agents.
168.titel: Read the real error message with result()
168.kurztext: If a flow fails at night, the reason is in the run history. The people who need to know often cannot open it. The result() function gets you the details: result('Try') returns an array with all top-level actions of the scope Try, each with name, status, code and, for failures, an error object with the message. In an action that only runs on has failed, you filter the array with Filter array for status equal to Failed. You get the text with first(body('Filter_array'))?['error']?['message'] and send it by email. result() only works with a Scope, Apply to each or Until. If the error sits deeper, you apply result() to the inner level.
168.wann_ja: When business users, admins or an agent need to know why a run failed.
168.wann_nein: For actions outside the scope. result() only sees what is inside the container.
168.fehler: Reading only the top level. Errors in a Condition or an inner Scope only appear in the result() of that level.

quiz.frage: According to the tip, which environment does For a selected item only run from?
antworten: The Default environment
Only Teams environments
Any production environment
erklaerungen: For a selected item only runs from the Default environment. If the flow lives in a production environment, you start it from a column-formatting button with executeFlow.

169.lernziel: You start flows from lists with a button without switching to premium.

quiz.frage: What does the action parameter control in the router flow?
antworten: Whether the flow needs a premium license
The language the agent answers in
The Switch to get, create or update
erklaerungen: The Switch on action routes to the get, create or update branch. The input parameter carries an OData filter or a JSON body for it.

170.lernziel: You give a Copilot Studio agent several tools with one flow.

quiz.frage: What does a run do that finds the IsRunning flag set to Yes?
antworten: It ends without processing anything
It sets the flag to No and starts over
It processes all emails once more
erklaerungen: If IsRunning is Yes, another run already owns the batch. The run ends with Terminate and the status Succeeded, without touching any emails.

171.lernziel: You bundle many trigger events into a single processing run.

quiz.frage: Why can't an agent correct errors from a directly bound connector itself?
antworten: Agents cannot use connectors in Copilot Studio
Connectors only report errors by email to the owner
Error statuses abort before the model sees the message
erklaerungen: Any status outside 2xx becomes the hard failure connectorRequestFailure before the language model reads the response. Only a flow that always returns readable JSON makes the error visible to the agent.

174.lernziel: You build agent tools that learn from errors.

quiz.frage: What do you change in the URL to open the hidden export page?
antworten: Append /edit to the end of the address
Append ?export=true to the address
Replace /details with /export
erklaerungen: On the flow's details page, replace /details at the end of the address with /export. The export page for the .zip package then opens.

193.lernziel: You export a single flow even without a visible button.

quiz.frage: What is the built-in version history not enough for?
antworten: Restoring an earlier saved version
Recovering a flow that was deleted entirely
Viewing older versions of an existing flow
erklaerungen: The version history only covers flows that still exist. For a deleted flow you need a backup, for example a regular solution export.

restore-earlier-version-flow-power-autom.lernziel: You restore an earlier flow version and know when you also need a backup.

quiz.frage: Which setting makes the Teams message come from you instead of the Flow bot?
antworten: Adding more recipients to the chat
Setting Post as to "Flow bot"
Setting Post as to "User"
erklaerungen: With Post as "User", the action "Post message in a chat or channel" posts in the name of the account behind the Teams connection. With "Flow bot", the message comes from the bot.

send-1-1-message-flow-teams.lernziel: You send a personal 1:1 message in Teams from a flow, with yourself as the sender.

quiz.frage: A flow without a trigger condition checks its condition only during the run. What happens on a change that does not match?
antworten: The flow does not start, SharePoint filters first
SharePoint reverts the change to the item
The flow starts anyway and consumes a run
erklaerungen: Without a trigger condition the flow starts on every change and checks afterwards. A SharePoint Automate Rule or a trigger condition filters first and saves the run.

power-automate-flows-vs-automate-rules.lernziel: You choose between Automate Rule, flow and trigger condition to avoid unnecessary runs.

quiz.frage: Why can you fill a Word template this way without the premium Word connector?
antworten: Because Word fills placeholders itself on opening
Because SharePoint converts Word files into text
Because a .docx file is a ZIP archive of XML
erklaerungen: A .docx file is a ZIP archive of XML files. You extract it, replace the placeholder in word/document.xml and zip it again.

fill-and-sign-word-document-power-apps-a.lernziel: You fill a Word template with standard actions through the XML in the archive.

quiz.frage: Why do you need a separate StateLog list for the progress display?
antworten: Because Power Apps cannot start flows directly
Because Respond to PowerApps can only answer once
Because a timer can only read SharePoint lists
erklaerungen: Respond to PowerApps answers only once. That is why the flow writes its progress to a StateLog list, which a timer in the app reads regularly.

how-to-track-the-current-progress-of-a-f.lernziel: You show the progress of a running flow in an app through a status list.

quiz.frage: Whose permissions does a SharePoint action in the flow use?
antworten: Those of the account behind the stored connection
Always those of the account that triggers the flow
Administrator rights, granted automatically
erklaerungen: Each action uses the connection that was set up when the flow was built. If it belongs to a service account, the action runs with its permissions, no matter who triggers the flow in the app.

power-apps-elevated-permissions-power-au.lernziel: You give app users elevated permissions for exactly one operation through a flow.

quiz.frage: How do you return an array from a flow to Power Apps?
antworten: As an array output of Respond to a Power App or flow
Not without premium, arrays only work with the Response action
As a JSON text output, parsed in the app with ParseJSON
erklaerungen: Respond to a Power App or flow only returns flat values. You send the array as JSON text and turn it back into a table in the app with ParseJSON.

return-an-array-from-powerautomate-to-po.lernziel: You return lists from a flow to an app without premium.

quiz.frage: What applies when the same flow sits in several solutions?
antworten: Each solution holds an independent copy
The flow is turned off in all solutions
It stays one flow, changes apply everywhere
erklaerungen: A flow can sit in several solutions and still remains one single flow. If you change or restore it, that applies in all solutions.

how-to-restore-create-backup-flow.lernziel: You back up flows through solutions so you can even bring back deleted flows.

quiz.frage: Which functions do you combine to read cells of an HTML table from an email?
antworten: concat() and join()
json() and first()
xml() and xpath()
erklaerungen: xml() turns the email's HTML into XML, and xpath() selects rows and cells in it. Ending the path with /text() gives you plain values.

extract-html-table-email-power-automate.lernziel: You read tables from HTML emails with xml() and xpath().
